messages.subject: question about 'iid'
parts:
Hey,

I'm pretty new to INLA, and this question may be very basic.

To tranfer the following code from Winbugs to INLA, I wrote:

y = c(130, 130)
i = 1:2
res = inla(y ~ f(i, model = 'iid', hyper = list(theta = list(prior = "normal", param = c(120, 0.01)), prec = 1/25)), data = data.frame(y,i), control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))

Winbugs code:
model {
   y[1] <- 130
   y[2] <- 130
   tau <- 1/pow(5, 2)

   for(i in 1:2) {
      y[i] ~ dnorm(theta, tau)
   }

  theta ~ dnorm(120, prec)
  prec <- 1/100
  ypred ~ dnorm(theta, tau)
}

I'm not sure if the INLA code is right or not, and I don't not how to get the predict values as 'ypred' in the Winbugs.

Many thanks for your kindly help!

Michelle

On Sun, 2013-04-14 at 07:21 -0700, Zishan Cui wrote:
> Hey,

> I'm pretty new to INLA, and this question may be very basic.

I think this is what you want. note that you get 'theta.pred' and not
ypred. you need then to add the gaussian noise with prec tau. (as far as
I recall the second argument to dnorm(,) in bugs is the precision....)

Best
H

> Winbugs code:
> model {
> y[1] <- 130
>
> y[2] <- 130
> tau <- 1/pow(5, 2)
>
>
> for(i in 1:2) {
> y[i] ~ dnorm(theta, tau)
> }
>
>
> theta ~ dnorm(120, prec)
>
> prec <- 1/100
> ypred ~ dnorm(theta, tau)

y = c(130, 130, NA)
theta = rep(1, 3)
off = c(120, 120, 120)
res = inla(y ~ offset(off) + f(theta, model = 'iid',
hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1/100), fixed = TRUE))),
family = "gaussian",
control.family = list(
hyper = list(
prec = list(initial = log(5^2), fixed = TRUE))),
data = data.frame(y, off, theta),
control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))

theta.pred = res$marginals.linear.predictor[[3]]
plot(theta.pred)
lines(inla.smarginal(theta.pred))


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

The summary:
res$summary.fitted.values[3,]
and the marginal posterior distribution
plot(res$marginals.fitted.values[[3]], type='l')

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] question about 'iid'
parts:
On Sat, 2013-04-20 at 20:54 -0700, Yunlong Nie wrote:
> Following this question, I noticed that there are about 73 posterior
> samples in res$summary.fitted.values[3,]. I wonder if Inla can control
> the number of posterior samples in its output. Is 73 is a default
> setting?

what you want to do is like this:


y.pred.samples = rnorm(1000, mean = inla.rmarginal(1000,theta.pred), sd=
5)

hist(y.pred.samples, prob=T,n=100)



--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
